details:
FieldShift – From Space to Soil

NASA-Powered Smart Agriculture & Crop Rotation Decision Support System

NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026
Challenge: Field Shift – Adapting Farms with NASA Data

Executive Summary

Agriculture is increasingly affected by climate variability, changing rainfall patterns, rising temperatures, water scarcity, and soil sustainability challenges. Farmers need accessible information and practical tools to understand these environmental changes and make informed crop planning decisions.

FieldShift is an interactive, NASA-powered agricultural decision-support platform that transforms Earth observation data into understandable insights for sustainable farming.

The platform integrates NASA POWER historical climate information with NASA GIBS satellite imagery and environmental visualization resources, including MODIS vegetation imagery, GPM IMERG precipitation visualization, and SMAP soil-moisture visualization.

FieldShift provides interactive farm mapping, rainfall and temperature analysis, soil information inputs, crop suitability comparisons, alternative crop rotation exploration, water conservation recommendations, and climate scenario simulations.

One of its central capabilities is the Smart Crop Rotation Explorer, which allows farmers to compare existing and alternative crop sequences using environmental factors, crop requirements, and adjustable farmer priorities.

The platform also includes a farmer-oriented dashboard with interactive visualizations, climate comparisons, and downloadable agricultural reports.

Innovation

FieldShift connects space-based environmental observations with agricultural decision support. Rather than simply presenting satellite images or historical weather information, it creates a workflow that helps users explore the relationship between climate conditions, crop characteristics, water requirements, and sustainable crop rotation strategies.

Expected Impact

The project aims to improve access to environmental information, promote climate-aware crop planning, encourage water conservation, and increase awareness of sustainable soil-management practices.

Technology

HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, Leaflet.js, OpenStreetMap, NASA POWER API, NASA GIBS, and Python.

Vision

FieldShift aims to make advanced Earth observation information accessible to everyday farmers and encourage more informed, sustainable, and climate-resilient agricultural decisions.

From Space to Soil – Turning NASA Data into Smarter Farming Decisions.

FieldShift is an independent educational hackathon project and is not officially endorsed by NASA.
